system_overview: This specification models the abstract Synod consensus protocol, originally described by Lamport as the foundation for Paxos-family algorithms. The Synod protocol allows N processes to agree on a single chosen value from a set of possible inputs, even in the presence of process failures. A process can propose a value and may later output a chosen value, or it can fail and restart with a new input. The protocol guarantees that at most one value is ever chosen.
actors_and_components: The system consists of N processes (numbered 1 through N). Each process has an input value and can produce an output. An inner specification module tracks a global chosen value and the set of all input values ever proposed. Processes can choose (output a value) or fail (reset and start with a new input).
state_variables: The system tracks: (1) An input mapping from each process to its current proposed input value. (2) An output mapping from each process to either a chosen value or a special indicator meaning no output yet. Internally, the specification also tracks: (3) A chosen value (initially a special no-output indicator). (4) The set of all input values that any process has ever proposed (accumulated across failures and restarts).
initial_state: Each process starts with a nondeterministically chosen input from the set of valid inputs. All outputs are set to the no-output indicator. No value has been chosen yet. The set of all inputs is initialized to the set of initial inputs across all processes.
actions: Two actions per process: (1) Choose: A process that has not yet produced output selects a value to output. If no value has been globally chosen yet, the process nondeterministically selects any value from the set of all inputs ever proposed, sets that as the globally chosen value, and outputs it. If a value has already been chosen, the process outputs that value. (2) Fail: A process resets its output to the no-output indicator, nondeterministically selects a new input value from the valid inputs, and adds it to the accumulated set of all inputs. The chosen value is not affected by failures.
safety_properties: Consensus safety: At most one value is ever chosen. Any process that produces output must output the same chosen value. A chosen value must have been proposed by some process at some point.
model_bounds: N is declared as a constant positive natural number. The set of valid inputs is a constant. For model checking, these must be instantiated with finite values.
additional_assumptions: The specification uses existential quantification over internal variables (the chosen value and accumulated input set) to hide implementation details. The Synod specification serves as an abstract specification that concrete algorithms (like DiskSynod) are proven to implement.
